Yes, that does exactly what I hoped. Clicking the highlighted clock on "A field guide to ancient libraries" took it right off the Read later list, the count dropped, and the message said "marked as read and removed from the list" — so there's no ambiguity about what just happened. That keeps the pile honest: once I've read something, it's gone from there and the number actually means something.

And using the same clock to toggle it back off, rather than a separate "Done" button, feels natural to me — it's the same little control I used to put it there, so flipping it off to say "read it" is intuitive and there's less clutter on the card. Good call. Read later is settled for me — flag with one click, see just those, and clear them as I read.
